The cart. Add support for stacking percentage and flat discounts in src/cart/total.py, applied in a fixed order so results are deterministic. Requirements: percentage discounts must apply before flat discounts; an edge case where a 100 percent discount plus a flat discount must never go below zero, clamped at 0.00; add a test in tests/test_total.py covering the clamp; update docs/cart.md describing the stacking order. The HTTP client. Add bounded retry with exponential backoff to src/api/client.py for GET requests only. Requirements: retry at most three times; an edge case where a 429 response must honour the Retry-After header when present; add a test in tests/test_client.py using a stubbed transport that fails twice then succeeds; update docs/api.md with the retry policy. Keep the existing request method signature unchanged so callers in src/api/orders.py need no edits. Backoff should start at 100ms and double each attempt with no jitter. Do not retry POST or DELETE requests. Surface the final exception unchanged after retries are exhausted. Add a module level constant MAX_RETRIES. Run tests/test_client.py after the change.

The date utils. Add a parser for partial dates in src/util/dates.py that accepts YYYY, YYYY-MM and YYYY-MM-DD. Requirements: return a date object with missing components defaulting to January and day one; an edge case where February 30 must raise ValueError rather than roll over; add a test in tests/test_dates.py covering the invalid leap day; update docs/dates.md listing supported formats. Keep the existing parse_date name and signature so callers in src/report/monthly.py need no edits. Use datetime under the hood, no third party libraries. Reject whitespace padded input by stripping before parsing. Return a clear error message naming the bad input. Run tests/test_dates.py after the change.
requirements: defaulting to January and day one

The notification scheduler. Add digest batching to src/notify/digest.py so multiple queued notifications for the same user are merged into a single summary email instead of one email each. The batcher collects items in a five minute window, groups them by user id, and emits one rendered digest per group. Add a helper build_digest(items) that returns the merged subject and body. Cover the edge case where a user has exactly one item: still send a normal single notification, not a digest. Existing templates must not change. Add tests in tests/test_digest.py for grouping and the single item case. Document the window and the batching rule in docs/notifications.md.

Cover the edge case of non-ASCII and emoji characters: count them as letters rather than penalising the input. The function should run in constant time relative to the password contents it inspects. Add tests in tests/test_strength.py covering each score band and the unicode case. Document the scoring bands in docs/auth.md.
